players.product: commercial & industrial electrical contracting for data centers

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Kelly Huntington: second quarter 2026 revenues were a record $1.08 billion, an increase of $181 million or 20% year over year; T&D revenues were $524 million (+4%), with work under master service agreements approximately 65% of T&D revenues; C&I revenues were $558 million, a record for the segment and up 42%, primarily on higher revenue on fixed-price contracts.
quarterly_data.figure: $1.08 billion Q2 2026 revenue, +20% year over year (C&I $558 million +42%, T&D $524 million +4%)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Kelly Huntington: gross margin was 13.2% in Q2 2026 vs 11.5% a year earlier, on better-than-anticipated productivity, favorable job closeouts and increased scope, partly offset by inefficiencies on certain projects; T&D operating income margin 9.4% (8% a year earlier); C&I operating income margin 8.5% (5.6%), also helped by projects progressing at higher contractual margins, some nearing completion; SG&A $74 million, up approximately $11 million mainly on incentive compensation; net income a record $50 million (vs $27 million); diluted EPS $3.17, up 86% from $1.70; EBITDA a record $85 million (vs $56 million).
quarterly_data.figure: 13.2% gross margin; net income $50 million; diluted EPS $3.17; EBITDA $85 million

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Kelly Huntington: total backlog as of June 30, 2026 was a record $3.16 billion, 20% higher than a year ago, consisting of $1.27 billion for the T&D segment and $1.89 billion for the C&I segment.
quarterly_data.figure: $3.16 billion backlog, 20% higher year over year (T&D $1.27 billion, C&I $1.89 billion)

quarterly_data.signal: T&D COO Brian Stern: The L.E. Myers Co. was awarded two large transmission jobs for Xcel Energy with a combined value in excess of $200 million. CEO Rick Swartz: both projects were added to backlog this quarter, as anticipated for the past six to eight months; he expects their revenue to start burning in the second half of 2027 ('There's a chance material could come in a little sooner') and then continue burning over an 18-month period.
quarterly_data.figure: in excess of $200 million (two transmission jobs); revenue burn starting second half of 2027

quarterly_data.signal: T&D COO Brian Stern: other Q2 T&D awards - Sturgeon Electric was selected for a 500 kV substation project in Arizona; Great Southwestern Construction was awarded a 345 kV transmission rebuild project in Texas plus a greenfield substation project in Colorado and additional substation work in New Mexico; Harlan was awarded a substation expansion project in Ohio and several distribution projects in Pennsylvania; steady bidding activity in T&D markets.

C&I COO Don Egan: MYR Group was awarded data center work in New Jersey and Arizona, multiple data center projects in Colorado, aerospace work in California, and hospitality and higher education work in New York; C&I bidding activity remained healthy and backlog continued to grow; sustained investment in data centers, grid modernization, power infrastructure and industrial facilities reinforces a healthy backdrop for electrical contracting, particularly mission-critical facilities.

CEO Rick Swartz on C&I mix: 'data centers isn't the number one market in every geographic area we're in'; good activity across all five or six key markets, including advanced manufacturing and transportation; 'we're not going to focus just on data centers. We like data centers.' He sees C&I projects being budgeted for construction in 2028, 2029, 2030 and calls it 'a very robust market'.

CEO Rick Swartz: full-year projections unchanged - operating margins expected in the mid part of the C&I range of 6%-9% and the mid-range of the T&D range of 8%-11% ('We'd love to see an uptick from there'); overall growth 'probably in that 13%-15%' on an organic basis, with the Valley acquisition adding roughly $250 million of revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: C&I operating margin mid-range of 6%-9%; T&D mid-range of 8%-11%; organic growth probably 13%-15%

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Rick Swartz: on July 1 MYR Group closed the acquisition of Valley Electric and Comet Electric, expanding its commercial and industrial capabilities and geographic presence, with extensive prefabrication capabilities; he is pleased with the speed of integration and calls the acquisition's performance 'as projected'. CFO Kelly Huntington: expected revenue contribution in the approximately $250 million range for the rest of the year, with a more neutral contribution to EPS and operating income in the first year because of higher backlog amortization.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately $250 million revenue contribution for the rest of 2026

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Rick Swartz on high-voltage transmission: well-aligned with 345, 500 and even some 765 kV work, but does not see that work starting until the second half of 2027 and beyond - 765 kV projects 'at best case, the end of 2027, but more likely 2028 and beyond' as customers work through siting issues; the company is budgeting and doing constructability for projects constructing in 2028 and beyond, 'clear out into the 30s'.
quarterly_data.figure: 765 kV work at best case end of 2027, more likely 2028 and beyond

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Rick Swartz: 'We're starting to see a lot of markets tighten up a little bit' on labor, some areas tighter than others; customers' conversations remain around getting material on time and having labor aligned for construction; MYR Group is well-positioned from a labor standpoint; over 90% of the business is return clientele, with 'probably' more favorable terms and conditions today than in contracts eight months or a year ago. C&I COO Don Egan: 'we are not price makers'; it is still a competitive landscape.
quarterly_data.figure: over 90% of business is return clientele

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Kelly Huntington: Q2 2026 operating cash flow was $3 million (vs $33 million), on the timing of tax payments and of billings on project starts and completions; free cash flow was negative $26 million (vs positive $12 million) with higher capital expenditures to support future growth; 'We could see our DSOs going from the current mid-50s to more of the low to mid-60s' over the next few quarters as over-billings balance out, a headwind against strong EBITDA growth.
quarterly_data.figure: $3 million operating cash flow; free cash flow negative $26 million
